title: Quadratic pointing and background fits retain a 21 to 24 ppm component in KIC 10001893 Kepler Q11 to Q17
abstract: We test whether a quadratic response to measured pointing and sky background can account for the known 19.48-hour flux signal of KIC 10001893. We reuse 14 public Kepler release 25 quarters. A fixed early phase and frequency set the later test. Quadratic fits with coefficients constant for a quarter, 30 days or 15 days retain later components from 21.38 to 24.37 parts per million. With 3-day trends, the 15-day response gives 24.37 +/- 5.67 ppm and a paired change of +1.34 +/- 3.01 ppm from the reference fit. Errors assume independent 6-day noise blocks and fixed early phase. At least 94.79 percent of pooled harmonic design information remains. Direct synthetic fits and exact tone increments pass numerical checks. These restricted nonlinear instrument models do not remove the component. They do not confirm a planet or locate its source. No independent telescope data are used. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval steps are included; external observations remain separate.

display.caption: Later phase components after joint instrument fits. Bars are 1.96 conditional block standard errors. Q denotes a quarter; 30 and 15 denote response intervals in days. The models share observations and are dependent.
